summary: fastapi.File(max_size=...) silently ignored, no upload size enforcement
failure_scenario: Client uploads 5GB file; max_size=50MB is not a valid FastAPI File() parameter and falls into **extra/dropped silently; server reads entire file into memory via f.write() in async endpoint; OOM crash or disk exhaustion

summary: task_done() called after re-queuing task on session-loss, breaking Queue.unfinished_count invariant
failure_scenario: get() increments unfinished→1, session lost triggers put() back to queue, task_done() decrements unfinished→0; task still in queue but counter is zero; graceful shutdown's Queue.join() returns immediately, discarding the re-queued unprocessed task

summary: DB pending record inserted before task_queue availability check, creating orphaned records on queue failure
failure_scenario: During startup/shutdown race, add_pending_record() succeeds writing status='pending' to DB; subsequent task_queue.get() returns None; API returns error but DB record remains as pending forever; pollutes count_pending_retry_records and stats overview

summary: API server lifespan shutdown only sleep(2) before closing browser/DB, no graceful task queue drain
failure_scenario: Upload in progress (up to 120s UPLOAD_TIMEOUT); SIGTERM received; stop_event.set() + sleep(2) + browser.close() + db.close(); daemon UploadProcessor thread killed mid-operation; DB records stuck in 'processing' state permanently; contrast with main.py which drains queue up to 30s before shutdown

summary: _process_miniprogram_task already_handled branch overwrites specific error_message from _handle_failure with generic one
failure_scenario: _handle_failure writes specific error like 'XX(session lost)'; already_handled branch reads last_upload_error (empty for non-upload-stage failures like BROWSER_INIT/SCHOOL_CHECK); calls update_record_structured_error overwriting specific error with generic 'upload operation failed'; root cause lost

summary: get_stats_overview() counts pending records in denominator, deflating reported success_rate
failure_scenario: 10 success + 5 miniprogram pending records; SELECT COUNT(*) = 15; success_rate = 10/15 = 66.7%; actual rate for non-pending tasks is 100%; stats overview API shows misleading low success rate

summary: API retry endpoint increments retry count and marks processing BEFORE queue check; stuck on failure
failure_scenario: retry_count incremented, retry_status set to 'processing', then task_queue.get() returns None; API returns error but unlike the max-retry branch (line 404) which sets status='finished', this path leaves status='processing' permanently; retry count was consumed for nothing

summary: Outer except handler in run() misses task_done(), causing Queue.join() to hang on unexpected exceptions
failure_scenario: _process_file or _process_miniprogram_task raises unhandled exception; caught by outer except at line 224; task_done() at line 218 never executes; Queue.unfinished_count stays >0; graceful shutdown's task_queue.join() hangs forever, preventing program exit

summary: _agent_retry_map dict shared across Agent and UploadProcessor threads without lock
failure_scenario: Agent thread calls register_agent_retry() writing to _agent_retry_map dict; UploadProcessor thread simultaneously reads/pops via _notify_agent_result or _preprocess_agent_retry; dict resize during write can interleave with read; potential KeyError, lost update, or partial data read under CPython GIL

summary: Browser idle monitor daemon thread may call db.count_pending_retry_records() after db.close() during shutdown
failure_scenario: Shutdown sequence: stop_event.set() → sleep(2) → db.close(); daemon monitor thread just entered loop body before event check; proceeds to call db.count_pending_retry_records() on closed connection; sqlite3.ProgrammingError: Cannot operate on a closed database

summary: Browser idle monitor logic duplicated ~100 lines verbatim between api_server.py and main.py
failure_scenario: Same monitoring loop (idle check→timeout check→crash detection→login check) with same 3 dedup flags exists in both api_server.py:110-192 and main.py:66-169; any bugfix to monitoring logic must be applied in two places or they will drift; belongs on BrowserAutomation as shared method

Both methods independently implement parse→read→classify→upload→handle_result pipeline; only difference is how school/grade/subject are obtained; success handling diverges (one uses _on_upload_success, other inlines DB writes); failure handling diverges (one delegates to _handle_failure, other writes DB directly); bugfix to pipeline must be applied in 2 places

summary: POST /api/report/generate reads start_date/end_date as query params instead of Form/Body
failure_scenario: Client sends POST with JSON body {start_date, end_date} expecting standard POST semantics; FastAPI treats plain str params on POST as query parameters; returns 422 validation error; inconsistent with /api/upload/submit which correctly uses Form(...)

summary: Blocking sync f.write(content) in async endpoint freezes asyncio event loop during file uploads up to 50MB
failure_scenario: async def submit_upload calls synchronous f.write(content) on main thread; 50MB write blocks event loop 200-500ms (SSD) to 1-2s (HDD); during this window all other API requests are unserved; concurrent uploads serialize on the event loop

summary: error_context initialized as {} stays empty on folder parse failure path; JSON column stores NULL
failure_scenario: error_context = {}; folder parse fails; _handle_failure called with error_context={}; inside _handle_failure, bool({}) is False so json.dumps skipped, error_context column gets NULL; folder_name is in its own column but structured error context is inconsistent with success path
